titleEn: I'm a Big Brother—I Can Help!

pages.text: "Grandpa, watch me!" Nils the little bear hopped by the stove. Grandpa Bruno looked only into a box. "Shh. The baby bird is asleep." Nils's raised paws slowly fell. His chest hurt a little.
In the box was a chick that had fallen from its nest. Grandpa had found it that morning. "I hate the bird! You only like the bird!" Nils stamped, then raced up to the loft.
The loft was dim; only the ladder opening was bright. Below came cheeping and Grandpa's "There, there." Nils gripped his covers. "Grandpa, won't you look at me?"
Then Grandpa climbed up and drew back the covers. "You're a big brother now. There's a job that needs a big brother's paws." He held Nils's paws warmly. "Shall we do it together?"
They stood side by side before the box. The chick cheeped. "Why is it crying?" Nils looked quietly. "Um... Is the hard floor making it cold?" The chick shivered.
Nils put his own soft moss cushion in the box. The chick nestled into it and stopped crying. A touch of its beak to his paw chased the hateful feeling away.
"Grandpa! The cushion made it stop!" Nils stood proud. "I'm a big brother—I can help! I'll look after the cushion!" Behind his glasses, Grandpa smiled.
When Nils sang, the chick bobbed its head. It looked only at Nils. "Beside the box is the most fun place now." He rested his chin on its edge.
Nils called, "One, cold means cushion! Two, crying means song! Three, sleeping means shh!" Now he didn't sulk when Grandpa watched the box. Both paws high! "I'm a big brother—I can help!"
Grandpa hugged Nils. "Thanks to your cushion, the baby will sleep soundly!" A little one brings something for your paws to do. Nils whispered to the box, "I'm a big brother—I can help! Good night."
